explanations: terra: God teaches Adam ٱلْأَسْمَآءَ كُلَّهَا; names make the created things knowable, directly illustrating the dictionary account of a name as what identifies an essence.
terra: Adam discloses the beings' names while God declares knowledge of the heavens' and earth's unseen, linking naming as disclosure to what remains hidden.

luna: The section’s k-b-r family distinguishes divine greatness from a creature’s self-importance; this verse says Iblis refused and grew arrogant, the original scene of a creature resisting God’s command through claimed rank.

luna: The section’s d-n-w gloss includes what is low or lesser, and its central choice is the lower life over the better Hereafter; this verse uses “أدنى” for the inferior thing chosen in place of what is better, a concrete but worldly-food instance of that lower-for-better exchange. | terra: Moses asks whether the people would exchange what is lower for what is better, directly stating the value contrast carried by the section's discussion of أدنى.
terra: They purchase worldly life with the hereafter, turning the section's preference into an exchange and exposing the low value of what they buy.
terra: Preventing God's name from being remembered in places of worship and seeking their ruin is the precise reversal of raising houses for His name and tasbih.
terra: “Remember Me and I will remember you” makes remembrance reciprocal divine acknowledgment rather than a mere utterance, supporting dhikr's honor-bearing sense.
terra: وَلِتُكَبِّرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا هَدَىٰكُمْ makes magnifying God the response to His guidance, joining the section's greatness-language to the guidance of 87:3.

luna: The section’s s-m-w dictionary branch calls the crescent’s visible form “سماوة الهلال” when it rises a little above the horizon; this verse asks about the new moons and identifies them as visible time-markers. | terra: The ayah treats crescent forms as time-signs; it activates the section's dictionary picture of the hilal becoming distinct above the horizon, though the ayah itself does not describe its rising.
terra: After being told to remember God intensely, some people ask only for this world and have no share in the hereafter; low-life desire stands inside a remembrance scene.
terra: The balanced prayer asks for good in both this world and the hereafter and protection from Fire, correcting the one-horizon request in 2:200.
terra: God favors some messengers over others and raises some in degrees, presenting rank as His grant even among honored servants.

luna: The section’s al-ʿulūw axis belongs to the Lord; this verse closes by naming God “العلي العظيم,” coupling divine highness and greatness rather than a ruler’s self-claim. | terra: The Throne encompasses heavens and earth and God is ٱلْعَلِىُّ ٱلْعَظِيمُ; cosmic rule joins true elevation to magnificence.
terra: Abraham answers a ruler's claim over life and death by challenging him to bring the sun from the west; a creature's sovereignty fails at the horizon.

luna: The section presents the worldly life as a preferred, lesser good; this verse names the attractions that beautify it, calls them worldly enjoyment, and contrasts them with the good return with God. | terra: Desired possessions are presented as the adornment of worldly life, while the beautiful return is with God; attraction and destination are placed on different levels.
terra: The Prophet is told to announce what is better than worldly adornment: lasting gardens, purified spouses, and God's approval.
terra: God gives and removes rule and grants honor or humiliation as He wills; the two-direction movement denies rulers ownership of their height.
terra: Remembering the Lord much and glorifying Him morning and evening places dhikr and tasbih in one divine instruction.
terra: God tells Jesus that He will raise him to Himself and purify him from the disbelievers, joining elevation to divine action and purification.

terra: تَعَالَوْا۟ نَدْعُ أَبْنَآءَنَا uses the dictionary's “come up” form for a summons to a decisive mutual invocation; the lexical history supplies the vertical undertone, though the ayah does not state height.

luna: The section’s ʿ-l-w dictionary branch says “تعال” originally calls someone to a high place; here the call is “تعالوا إلى كلمة سواء,” shifting that upward invitation into a summons to a shared word about worshiping God alone. | terra: تَعَالَوْا۟ إِلَىٰ كَلِمَةٍۢ سَوَآءٍ calls people upward, in the dictionary history of تعال, toward a common word that no one take another as lords.
terra: وَأَنتُمُ ٱلْأَعْلَوْنَ ties being uppermost to faith and steadiness after defeat, paralleling the divinely granted superiority of Moses.
terra: Those who desire the reward of this world and those who desire the reward of the hereafter are explicitly distinguished, making preference a chosen horizon of recompense.
terra: تَعَالَوْا۟ قَٰتِلُوا۟ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ summons the hypocrites into costly duty, but their retreat reveals the distance between verbal nearness and moral ascent.

luna: The section’s low/near worldly pole is measured against what endures; this verse calls worldly life a deceptive enjoyment and locates success in being saved from the Fire and admitted to the Garden.
terra: The domestic warning closes إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيًّۭا كَبِيرًۭا, placing every exercise of human authority beneath God's height and greatness.
terra: تَعَالَوْا۟ إِلَىٰ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ وَإِلَى ٱلرَّسُولِ is an upward-form call toward revelation, while hypocrites turn decisively away.
terra: Those who sell worldly life for the hereafter are summoned to struggle, reversing the exchange made by people who buy the low life.
terra: مَتَٰعُ ٱلدُّنْيَا قَلِيلٌۭ وَٱلْءَاخِرَةُ خَيْرٌۭ declares the worldly enjoyment little and the hereafter better, directly interpreting the high-low valuation.
terra: Whoever wants worldly reward is reminded that the rewards of both this world and the hereafter are with God, setting a boundary against treating nearness as the only available good.
terra: Hypocrites occupy the lowest depth of the Fire, the direct downward opposite of the highest degrees promised to faithful workers.
terra: Rather than Jesus being mastered by his enemies, God raised him to Himself; creaturely plots are bounded by divine elevation.
terra: The call تَعَالَوْا۟ إِلَىٰ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ is refused for inherited ancestral ways, staging the etymological upward invitation against settled human custom.

luna: The section’s “الدنيا” is the lesser, near life; this verse contrasts the worldly life’s play and amusement with the Hereafter, which it calls better for the God-conscious. | terra: Worldly life is play and diversion, while the final abode is better for the God-fearing; fear redirects value away from the low life.
terra: Abraham sees the moon بَازِغًۭا and then setting; the crescent or orb emerging at the horizon becomes a test of whether visible height deserves lordship.
terra: The rising sun is called هَٰذَآ أَكْبَرُ, yet its setting disproves its lordship; apparent celestial greatness is measured against the enduring Lord.
terra: After the setting lights, Abraham turns to the creator of the heavens and earth, transferring devotion from high visible forms to their Maker.
terra: After Abraham rejects setting lights as lords, God says He raises in degrees whom He wills; true elevation is bestowed after false celestial lordship is refused.
terra: After people invent partners and children for God, سُبْحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ clears and exalts Him above their descriptions, precisely enacting the prose's definition of tasbih.
terra: تَعَالَوْا۟ أَتْلُ مَا حَرَّمَ رَبُّكُمْ uses the height-derived invitation to summon hearers toward the Lord's concrete moral boundaries.

luna: The section contrasts Pharaoh’s claimed highness with true rank; this verse says God made people successors and raised some above others in degrees as a test, presenting elevation as assigned and accountable. | terra: God makes people successors on earth and raises some above others in degrees to test them, defining worldly elevation as probation rather than possession.
luna: The section links corrupted height to arrogance; Iblis answers the command to prostrate by claiming he is better than Adam, a direct self-ranking rather than bestowed elevation.

luna: The section warns that ʿ-l-w can turn into self-exaltation; God rebukes Iblis’s arrogance and orders him to descend, making the high/low reversal explicit. | terra: Iblis is ordered down because the place is not for self-magnification and is expelled among the abased; assumed height produces literal and moral descent.

luna: The section contrasts a ruler’s earthly self-exaltation with genuine elevation; this verse says heaven’s gates will not open to those who deny God’s signs and act arrogantly, setting a boundary on their claimed ascent.
terra: The supposed gods are only names coined by people and their fathers without divine authority; bare naming fails to raise a nonexistent referent into lordship.
terra: When divine manifestation crushes the mountain, Moses falls and wakes saying سُبْحَٰنَكَ; creaturely height collapses before the splendor to which tasbih responds.

luna: The section’s ʿ-l-w gloss warns of arrogant rising on earth; this verse says God turns away from His signs those who act arrogantly in the land, a direct boundary between self-exaltation and receiving guidance. | terra: Those who seek greatness on earth without right are turned from God's signs, showing how self-elevation blocks the reminder that could raise them rightly.
terra: The heirs of scripture take the goods of “this lower/nearer” existence while presuming forgiveness, an explicit adjectival use of أدنى for morally cheap present gain.

luna: The section says the name identifies its bearer and raises the named one’s mention; this verse assigns the most beautiful names to God and commands calling on Him by them. | terra: The most beautiful names belong to God and are the means by which He is called; deviation in those names is condemned, guarding rightful naming.
terra: The armies occupy ٱلْعُدْوَةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا and ٱلْعُدْوَةِ ٱلْقُصْوَىٰ, using the root in its concrete “nearer bank” sense and displaying the spatial axis behind الدنيا.
terra: People take religious leaders and the Messiah as lords besides God; glorifying Him above their association clears the title “Lord” of creaturely seizure.

luna: The section says the name “الدنيا” can carry nearness and lesser worth; this rebuke asks whether people are content with the worldly life in place of the Hereafter and calls its enjoyment small by comparison. | terra: أَرَضِيتُم بِٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا مِنَ ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ asks whether people are satisfied with the low life in exchange for the hereafter and calls its enjoyment little.
terra: God makes the disbelievers' word ٱلسُّفْلَىٰ and His own word ٱلْعُلْيَا; the section's high-low axis becomes a judgment between rival claims.
terra: After gardens and dwellings are promised, God's approval is called greater; divine pleasure outranks even the created reward.

luna: The section’s s-m-w dictionary branch evokes the crescent becoming visible above the horizon; this verse says the moon has measured phases, giving the crescent a place in the recurring lunar cycle and its timekeeping use.
terra: Those satisfied and at ease with worldly life ignore God's signs; contentment with nearness is presented as the decisive misvaluation.
terra: Fire is the refuge earned by the people described in 10:7, joining satisfaction with the low life to the fire-end named in the section.
terra: God is declared glorified and exalted above the intercessors people associate with Him; transcendence removes a false heavenly hierarchy.
terra: Worldly life is likened to rain-fed growth that reaches full adornment and is suddenly reduced as though it had not flourished yesterday, a close nonlexical parallel to passing pasture.

luna: The section connects false highness with Pharaoh; after Moses and Aaron bring clear signs, this verse says Pharaoh and his chiefs were arrogant, a repeated account of resistance to divinely backed truth.
terra: Pharaoh is لَعَالٍۢ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ and among the extravagant, another contextual use of “high” for oppressive worldly ascendancy.

luna: The section names the choice of the low worldly life; this verse describes those who desire the present life and its adornment, connecting that preference to deeds done for its reward. | terra: Whoever desires worldly life and its adornment may be paid fully in it, making the chosen near horizon explicit.

luna: The section says the Hereafter is better and more enduring than worldly life; this neighbor completes 11:15 by saying what its seekers gain there and that they have no share in the Hereafter. | terra: Those confined to the desire in 11:15 have nothing in the hereafter but Fire; the distant consequence exposes the low value of the fulfilled near desire.
terra: The objects worshipped besides God are only names invented by people, while judgment belongs to God alone; the ayah separates labels from true lordship.
terra: The Prophet announces his clear path of calling to God and says وَسُبْحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ, joining missionary stance to clearing God of association.
terra: God raises the heavens without visible pillars and settles over the Throne, assigning literal cosmic elevation to the Creator.

luna: The section’s ʿ-l-w family includes exaltation and height; this verse calls God “المتعال” while describing His knowledge of unseen and seen, locating transcendence in the knower. | terra: God knows hidden and manifest and is ٱلْكَبِيرُ ٱلْمُتَعَالِ, uniting greatness with transcendence rather than with an earthly claim.
terra: Thunder glorifies God with praise and the angels do so in awe, placing tasbih in a visibly and audibly high atmospheric scene.

luna: The section says the worldly life is the lower choice beside what lasts; this verse describes people rejoicing in worldly life and calls its enjoyment small compared with the Hereafter. | terra: Expanded or measured provision belongs to God, and worldly life compared with the hereafter is only an enjoyment; provision and valuation meet in one claim.

luna: The section’s d-n-w gloss makes the worldly life the low or near choice, set against the better Hereafter; this verse describes people who prefer worldly life over the Hereafter and bar others from God’s way. | terra: Those who love worldly life over the hereafter also obstruct God's way, showing the directional consequence of preferring what is near.
terra: A good word is a good tree with firm root and branch in the sky, giving elevated speech a visible upward form and stable ground.
terra: A bad word is an uprooted tree with no stability, the downward and rootless counterpart to the ascending good word in 14:24.
terra: The Prophet is commanded to glorify his Lord with praise and to be among those who prostrate, joining exaltation of God to bodily lowering.

luna: The section defines tasbīḥ as declaring God above every evil; this verse announces God’s command and glorifies Him above what they associate with Him, a direct instance of that act. | terra: سُبْحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ begins the surah by combining glorification and exaltation against association.
terra: The arrogant are told to enter Hell's gates permanently, directly joining seized greatness to the fire-end of the section.
terra: Those who respond well receive good in this world, but the home of the hereafter is better; the ayah preserves worldly good while ranking the final home above it.

luna: The section assigns true highness to God and exposes self-claimed grandeur; this verse says the highest description belongs to God, setting divine measure against the deficient example it attributes to those who deny the Hereafter. | terra: Those without faith receive the evil description, while God has ٱلْمَثَلُ ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ; the highest description is reserved for Him.

luna: The section says the Hereafter is better and more enduring than the low worldly life; this verse contrasts what people possess and what is with God, saying the former ends while what is with God remains.

luna: The section frames “الدنيا” as the lower choice against what endures; this verse says they preferred the life of this world over the Hereafter, giving that preference its explicit comparative form. | terra: They preferred ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا عَلَى ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ, an exact statement of the section's choice with its proper object of comparison.
terra: The children of Israel are foretold to rise عُلُوًّۭا كَبِيرًۭا through corruption, combining the section's height and greatness roots in a blameworthy form.

luna: The section’s d-n-w gloss includes the nearest or first thing; this verse calls worldly desire “العاجلة” and contrasts its quickly bounded provision with the Hereafter, where the section locates what lasts. | terra: Whoever wants ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ receives only what God wills and then Hell, binding preference for immediacy to its limit and outcome.

luna: The section sets the low, near life against a better and enduring Hereafter; this neighbor completes 17:18 with the one who seeks the Hereafter and strives for it as a believer. | terra: Whoever wants the hereafter and strives for it in faith has the striving appreciated, giving the opposite orientation to 17:18.
terra: God extends His gift to both groups, showing that present provision does not by itself certify the height of either choice.
terra: The hereafter is أَكْبَرُ دَرَجَٰتٍۢ وَأَكْبَرُ تَفْضِيلًۭا; the low-life choice is corrected by greater ranks and greater preference beyond it.

luna: The section warns that al-ʿulūw can be corrupted into self-exaltation; this verse forbids walking arrogantly and sets the body’s limits against earth and mountains, a concrete boundary on human height. | terra: The arrogant walker cannot split the earth or reach the mountains in height, measuring human self-exaltation against physical limits it cannot cross.

luna: The section defines tasbīḥ as declaring God free of every evil and sets true divine highness against self-claimed grandeur; this verse glorifies and exalts God far above what they say, including their claim of great elevation. | terra: سُبْحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ ... عُلُوًّۭا كَبِيرًۭا combines transcendence, elevation, and greatness while clearing God of what people say, almost a lexical summary of the section.

luna: The section’s s-b-ḥ gloss defines glorification as declaring God pure; this verse says the heavens, earth, and all within them glorify Him, giving the command a cosmic scope. | terra: The seven heavens, earth, and everything in them glorify God; tasbih becomes the universal response of the entire high-low creation.

terra: When people demand that the Prophet ascend into heaven and bring down a book, he answers by glorifying his Lord and affirming that he is only a human messenger; claimed human ascent is bounded by divine transcendence.

luna: The section places the Lord’s name at the center of glorification; this verse permits calling God or the Most Merciful and says the most beautiful names belong to Him. | terra: Calling “Allah” or “the Merciful” reaches the same one to whom the beautiful names belong, making names disclose rather than divide their bearer.

luna: The section’s k-b-r gloss includes magnifying God with the takbīr; this command praises God as having no child or partner and calls for magnifying Him greatly, directing grandeur to its proper bearer. | terra: وَكَبِّرْهُ تَكْبِيرًۢا commands unqualified magnification of God after denying Him child, partner, and protecting patron, giving tesbih's content through takbir.

luna: The section contrasts remembrance of the Lord with preferring the low worldly life; this verse warns against following someone whose heart is heedless of remembrance and who follows desire, a specific opposite stance to the one who fears and remembers. | terra: The Prophet is told to remain with those calling their Lord and seeking His face, and not to let his eyes pass beyond them toward worldly adornment; remembrance and the low-life choice meet directly.
terra: Worldly life is rain-fed vegetation that becomes scattered dry matter; it gives the passing low life the same pasture-to-refuse trajectory present in Surah 87's context.

luna: The section says the near worldly life is surpassed by what is better and more enduring; this verse calls wealth and children adornments of worldly life, but says enduring good deeds are better with the Lord for reward and hope. | terra: Wealth and children are worldly adornment, but enduring good deeds are better with the Lord and better in hope, completing the passing scene in 18:45.
terra: The claim that God takes a son is answered by declaring Him transcendent; this gives the section's definition of tasbih a specific false description to remove.
terra: God grants Abraham's family لِسَانَ صِدْقٍ عَلِيًّۭا, a lofty truthful renown that realizes the section's link between mention and height.
terra: وَٱذْكُرْ فِى ٱلْكِتَٰبِ إِدْرِيسَ gives Idris remembered mention immediately before God raises him high in 19:57.

luna: The section makes al-aʿlā the image of elevation; this verse says God raised Idris to a high station, showing rank as something bestowed rather than claimed. | terra: وَرَفَعْنَٰهُ مَكَانًا عَلِيًّا says Idris was raised to a high station, a literal realization of honorable mention becoming elevation.
terra: After naming Him Lord of the heavens and earth and commanding worship, the ayah asks whether any سَمِيّ can be known for Him, protecting the uniqueness of the divine name.

luna: The section defines al-ʿulūw as height and explicitly turns to “the highest heavens”; this verse calls the heavens “العلى” and identifies their Creator as the source of the revelation. | terra: The revelation descends from the creator of ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ ٱلْعُلَى, locating creaturely height in heavens made by the Lord called Most High.

luna: The section cites the powerful figure standing before the highest horizon in 53:7; this preceding verse describes the figure as mighty and upright, while 53:7 supplies the horizon that completes the silhouette scene.

luna: The section’s first image glorifies the Lord’s name; this verse identifies God as the sole deity and says the most beautiful names are His, specifying the bearer of the names. | terra: ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ لَهُ ٱلْأَسْمَآءُ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ locates all beautiful names in the sole deity whose exaltation frames the surah.
terra: Moses sees a fire and hopes to find a brand or guidance at it; the same fire becomes the place where the Lord commands remembered prayer in 20:14.
terra: أَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ لِذِكْرِى directly binds remembrance of the speaking Lord to prayer, the same pair joined in 87:15.

luna: The section makes “الأعلى” the high pole of its axis; in the Moses–Pharaoh contest God tells Moses, “أنت الأعلى,” turning the title away from Pharaoh’s claim and toward God’s supported messenger. | terra: God tells the fearful Moses إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ; superiority is granted in the very confrontation where Pharaoh falsely claims the title for himself.

terra: The believing magicians tell Pharaoh لَن نُّؤْثِرَكَ, refusing the very act of preference used for choosing the low life in 87:16; their refusal begins the sequence that ends in the highest degrees.
terra: Within the magicians' reply, وَٱللَّهُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ states the same better-and-more-lasting judgment as 87:17 and explains why they will not prefer Pharaoh in 20:72.

luna: The section’s 87:12–13 describes the Fire as a punishment in which one neither dies nor lives; this verse gives that same suspended state for the criminal in Hell, and 20:75 supplies the contrasting high degrees of the believers. | terra: The criminal in Hell لَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا وَلَا يَحْيَىٰ exactly restages 87:13; here it stands immediately before the believers' high degrees.

luna: The section contrasts false self-exaltation with God-given elevation; after the magicians believe, this verse grants them “الدرجات العلى,” so genuine height is a reward for faith and righteous work, unlike Pharaoh’s claim in 79:24. | terra: The believer who comes with good works receives ٱلدَّرَجَٰتُ ٱلْعُلَىٰ, turning height from Pharaoh's claim into an awarded rank and completing the contrast with 20:74.

luna: The section calls the Hereafter better and more enduring than the low life; this neighbor completes the high degrees of 20:75 with lasting Gardens and the reward of one who purifies himself, echoing 87:14 and 87:17. | terra: The gardens are called the reward of مَن تَزَكَّىٰ, completing the 20:72-76 sequence with the purification that precedes remembered prayer in 87:14-15.

luna: The section’s ʿ-l-w root points to true height while warning that a ruler can corrupt it by self-exaltation; this verse declares God “تعالى,” the true King, locating sovereignty in God rather than a claimant such as Pharaoh. | terra: فَتَعَٰلَى ٱللَّهُ ٱلْمَلِكُ ٱلْحَقُّ gives true kingship and exaltation to God, directly answering the section's account of a king who “rose” by tyranny.
terra: The Prophet is commanded to glorify his Lord before sunrise and sunset and through the night, placing tasbih repeatedly along the horizon and daily arc.
terra: The flower of worldly life is a test, while وَرِزْقُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌۭ وَأَبْقَىٰ repeats the better-and-more-lasting counterweight to 87:16.
terra: The revealed book contains ذِكْرُكُمْ, plausibly both reminder and honored mention; this activates the section's secondary sense of dhikr as distinction.
terra: The imagined plurality of gods would ruin heaven and earth, so the Lord of the Throne is glorified above their descriptions.
terra: The claim that the Merciful has taken a child is answered سُبْحَٰنَهُۥ; the alleged children are instead honored servants, separating divine transcendence from granted honor.
terra: لِتُكَبِّرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا هَدَىٰكُمْ locates greatness in thankful worship rather than in the sacrificial bodies or human possession.
terra: Protected houses of worship are places where God's name is mentioned much; their preservation concretely sustains the raised-name space described in 24:36.

luna: The section joins al-ʿulūw and k-b-r, distinguishing God’s greatness from false self-exaltation; this verse calls God “العلي الكبير,” a direct divine pairing of the two axes. | terra: Because God is the Truth and rival invocations are false, He is ٱلْعَلِىُّ ٱلْكَبِيرُ; height and greatness follow exclusive lordship.
terra: Pharaoh and his chiefs act arrogantly and are قَوْمًا عَالِينَ, showing collective self-elevation in the Moses confrontation.

luna: The section’s tasbīḥ gloss is to declare God free of every evil; this verse denies God a child or partner and declares Him above what they describe, making that purification specific. | terra: The denial of a son or rival god ends سُبْحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ, making tasbih the clearing of the true Lord from creaturely descriptions.
terra: فَتَعَٰلَى ٱللَّهُ ٱلْمَلِكُ ٱلْحَقُّ repeats 20:114's true King formula and follows the denial that creation was purposeless.

luna: The section’s tasbīḥ gloss includes “نور” (light), which it links lexically to 87:12’s Fire; this verse calls God the Light of the heavens and earth, giving that light-family a divine illuminating use rather than the punitive Fire. | terra: The divine light parable contains a lamp kindled from a blessed tree and culminates in نُّورٌ عَلَىٰ نُورٍۢ; it supplies the light-fire majesty immediately before raised houses in 24:36.

luna: The section’s s-m-w “name” gloss says naming raises the named one’s mention; here houses are to be raised, the Lord’s name mentioned, and He glorified. This gathers 87:1 and 87:15 into one practice. | terra: The houses are permitted أَن تُرْفَعَ, God's name is remembered in them, and He is glorified there; one setting unites the section's raising, name, remembrance, and tasbih.
terra: Trade and sale do not distract these people from God's remembrance and prayer; their conduct in the raised houses of 24:36 reverses preference for the low life.
terra: God rewards the worshippers of 24:37 according to their best deeds and increases them from His bounty, supplying the higher return for leaving trade subordinate to remembrance.
terra: All beings in heaven and earth, including birds spread in flight, know their prayer and glorification; the raised houses of 24:36 belong within a wider cosmic worship scene.

luna: The section’s whole surah says of the condemned that they neither die nor live, while its tasbīḥ gloss exalts God; this verse commands glorification of the Ever-Living who does not die, a precise boundary between divine life and the Fire’s suspended state.
terra: Abraham asks for لِسَانَ صِدْقٍۢ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرِينَ, a truthful later renown; it supplies the prayer behind the lofty mention granted in 19:50.
terra: Moses sees a fire and hopes to bring news or a burning brand; this establishes the distant fire whose divine call and tasbih occur in 27:8.
terra: At the fire seen by Moses, the call blesses what is in and around it and says سُبْحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ, bringing fire, manifested splendor, and tasbih into one scene.
terra: At the fire Moses is told that the speaker is God, the Mighty, the Wise; the name identifies the Lord whose transcendence was declared in 27:8.
terra: Pharaoh's people reject signs ظُلْمًۭا وَعُلُوًّۭا despite inner certainty, defining their elevation as willful injustice rather than superior truth.

luna: The section’s ʿ-l-w gloss says a ruler’s rising in the land can mean tyranny and self-magnification; this verse says Pharaoh exalted himself in the land and divided its people, giving that corruption its political scene. | terra: إِنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ عَلَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ uses the exact corrupted sense developed in the prose: a ruler “rises” in the land by tyranny and division.
terra: Moses perceives a fire from the mountain and approaches for news or a brand, staging light seen at a distance before the divine naming in 28:30.
terra: From the fire-side tree Moses hears إِنِّىٓ أَنَا ٱللَّهُ رَبُّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ; the luminous scene discloses the true Lord by name.

luna: The section’s ʿ-l-w gloss describes a ruler rising in the land by tyrannizing and magnifying himself; Pharaoh’s claim to be the highest is paired here with his attempt to build a tower reaching toward the heavens. | terra: Pharaoh orders a tower fired from clay so that he might climb toward Moses' God; false lordship turns elevation and fire into a manufactured challenge.

luna: The section’s highness axis exposes the ruler who magnifies himself; this neighbor says Pharaoh and his forces were arrogant in the land, completing the tower scene of 28:38. | terra: Pharaoh and his troops exalt themselves in the land without right and deny their return, identifying the attitude behind the tower ordered in 28:38.
terra: God seizes Pharaoh and his troops and casts them into the sea, an abrupt downward reversal of the attempted ascent in 28:38-39.

luna: The section calls the worldly life the low or near pole and says the Hereafter is better and more lasting; this verse directly contrasts worldly enjoyment and adornment with what is better and more enduring with God. | terra: Worldly provision is temporary enjoyment and adornment, whereas what is with God is خَيْرٌۭ وَأَبْقَىٰ, explicitly decoding why the nearer life is lower.

luna: The section distinguishes the low life from what endures; this neighbor completes 28:60 by asking whether one promised a good promise to meet it is like one given worldly enjoyment and then brought to judgment. | terra: A person promised a good fulfillment is set against one merely given worldly enjoyment and then brought for judgment, separating lasting promise from present possession.
terra: Creation and choice belong to the Lord, then سُبْحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ removes the partners people elevate.

luna: The section defines worldly life as low and near against the Hereafter; this verse directs people to seek the Hereafter with what God has given them while not forgetting their share of this world, qualifying how the lower life may be used. | terra: The command to seek the final home with what God has given while not forgetting one's worldly share marks the boundary between ranking the hereafter higher and denying lawful present life.

luna: The section’s ʿ-l-w gloss warns that earthly rising can mean arrogant self-exaltation; this verse reserves the Hereafter for those who do not desire “علوا في الأرض” or corruption, the direct boundary to Pharaoh’s claim. | terra: The final home is assigned to those who do not desire عُلُوًّۭا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ; renouncing self-elevation becomes the way to the enduring higher outcome.
luna: The section’s ʿ-l-w gloss defines earthly rising as transgression and self-magnification; this verse names Qarun, Pharaoh, and Haman as arrogant in the land despite Moses’ clear proofs.
terra: وَلَذِكْرُ ٱللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ explicitly calls God's remembrance “greater,” joining the section's two lexical claims about dhikr and greatness.

luna: The section says the worldly life is low and the Hereafter better and lasting; this verse draws that boundary by calling this life play and amusement and the Hereafter the real life. | terra: Worldly life is diversion and play, whereas the final abode is ٱلْحَيَوَانُ, the true life; the “low life” is denied final claim even to fullness of life.

luna: The section’s d-n-w dictionary gloss includes what is nearest; this verse locates the Romans’ defeat in the nearest land, preserving that spatial sense of the root apart from the moral choice of worldly life. | terra: The Romans are defeated فِىٓ أَدْنَى ٱلْأَرْضِ, a concrete nearest/lower land use that preserves the spatial sense behind “the low/near life.”
terra: People know only the outward surface of worldly life while remaining heedless of the hereafter, making nearness also an epistemic limitation.

luna: The section ties al-aʿlā to the Creator; this verse says God originates and repeats creation and that the highest attribute belongs to Him in the heavens and earth. | terra: The highest description belongs to God in heavens and earth, and He is mighty and wise; divine height governs both realms.
terra: After asking whether alleged partners create, provide, kill, or revive, the ayah glorifies and exalts God above them, joining transcendence to uniquely divine acts.

luna: The section’s height and greatness axis points to God as its true bearer; this verse likewise says “العلي الكبير,” anchoring those qualities in divine truth and sovereignty. | terra: The contrast between God as Truth and false objects of invocation ends with وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلْعَلِىُّ ٱلْكَبِيرُ.
terra: True believers fall prostrate when reminded of the signs, glorify their Lord, and do not act arrogantly; low posture and tasbih directly reverse false height.
terra: ٱلْعَذَابِ ٱلْأَدْنَىٰ is set below ٱلْعَذَابِ ٱلْأَكْبَرِ, placing “nearer/lower” and “greater” at opposite ends of one punitive scale.
terra: The Prophet says فَتَعَالَيْنَ to wives who desire ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَزِينَتَهَا; the “come” form derived from height stands inside the same low-life choice.
terra: Choosing God, His Messenger, and the final home reverses the choice of worldly life in 33:28 and makes explicit what stands at the upper end of that decision.

luna: The section links remembrance of the Lord’s name with prayer and glorification; this command to believers to remember God much repeats the remembrance side of that pairing. | terra: ٱذْكُرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ ذِكْرًۭا كَثِيرًۭا makes abundant remembrance the believers' commanded stance.

luna: The section joins remembrance to glorifying the Lord; this neighbor completes 33:41 by commanding glorification morning and evening, giving the paired acts a daily rhythm. | terra: وَسَبِّحُوهُ completes the command of 33:41 by pairing remembrance with glorification, the same two motions joined across 87:1 and 87:15.

luna: The section’s al-ʿulūw and k-b-r roots make highness and greatness divine qualities; this verse names God “العلي الكبير” after fear leaves the hearts, joining divine greatness with reverence. | terra: After intercession is stripped from creatures except by permission, the divine speech is affirmed as truth and God as ٱلْعَلِىُّ ٱلْكَبِيرُ.
terra: The angels glorify God and disown the people who worshipped them, showing exalted servants refusing the divine rank humans projected onto them.

luna: The section’s s-m-w gloss makes a name an elevation of its bearer, while its dh-k-r gloss joins remembrance to honor; here the good word ascends to God and righteous work is raised, specifying how speech and action acquire height. | terra: إِلَيْهِ يَصْعَدُ ٱلْكَلِمُ ٱلطَّيِّبُ makes good speech ascend to God and righteous action raise it, giving a vertical scene for elevated name and remembrance.

luna: The section’s s-m-w branch specifically evokes the crescent rising above the horizon; this verse follows the moon’s phases until it returns like an old date-stalk, giving the crescent a concrete place in its cycle. | terra: The moon is measured through phases until it returns like an old palm stalk; its changing visible crescent supplies the celestial form used in the section's sumūw dictionary image.

luna: The section’s low/near and high poles can describe the sky as well as worldly life; this verse specifically calls the adorned heaven the nearest one, a spatial use of “الدنيا.” | terra: ٱلسَّمَآءَ ٱلدُّنْيَا means the nearest heaven; الدنيا here marks nearness within an explicitly elevated cosmic scene rather than worldly life.
terra: God is glorified above what people describe, a direct formulation of tasbih as clearing Him of every unworthy attribution.

luna: The section’s tasbīḥ gloss is God’s purification from every evil; this closing command glorifies the Lord of might above what they attribute, locating true majesty in God. | terra: سُبْحَٰنَ رَبِّكَ رَبِّ ٱلْعِزَّةِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ states explicitly that glorifying the Lord means clearing Him of their descriptions.
terra: وَٱلْقُرْءَانِ ذِى ٱلذِّكْرِ may carry honor as well as reminder, so it plausibly reflects the section's secondary “dhikr as distinction” sense, but the semantic choice is not explicit here.
luna: The section warns that highness can become self-exaltation; this verse says Iblis was arrogant and among the disbelievers, identifying the refusal behind a false claim to rank.

luna: The section distinguishes granted divine highness from self-claimed grandeur; God asks Iblis whether he was arrogant or among the exalted, making the claim to rank the issue of the command to prostrate. | terra: God asks Iblis أَسْتَكْبَرْتَ أَمْ كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلْعَالِينَ; assumed greatness and imagined membership among “the high” are exposed as refusal to bow.

luna: The section’s axis exposes self-awarded superiority; this neighbor gives Iblis’s reason for refusing, his claim that he is better because he was created from fire while Adam was created from clay.
terra: Hearts recoil when God alone is mentioned but rejoice when lesser objects are mentioned, exposing a reversed hierarchy of remembrance.
terra: The faces of those who lied about God are darkened, and Hell is named the lodging of the arrogant; false description and self-greatness meet their reversal.

luna: The section places God’s true highness above a creature’s self-claim; this verse rebukes people for failing to appraise God properly and depicts the earth held in His grasp and the heavens folded, setting divine scale beyond human grandeur. | terra: After measuring all creation within God's grasp, سُبْحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ clears Him above partners and exposes their failure to estimate His true greatness.
terra: At judgment the earth shines with the light of its Lord, giving divine splendor a cosmic scene rather than locating majesty in a creature's flame.
terra: The arrogant are commanded into Hell's gates for permanent residence, making their chosen height end in the worst lodging.
terra: Angels surround the Throne glorifying their Lord with praise as judgment is completed, locating tasbih around the highest emblem of rule.
terra: Those who believed when God alone was invoked but disbelieved when partners were named are judged by ٱللَّهِ ٱلْعَلِىِّ ٱلْكَبِيرِ.
terra: رَفِيعُ ٱلدَّرَجَٰتِ ذُو ٱلْعَرْشِ names God as high or raiser of degrees and possessor of the Throne, the source of every true rank.

luna: The section’s ʿ-l-w gloss makes a ruler’s self-raised status corrupt; here Pharaoh orders a tower so he might reach the routes to the heavens, turning claimed supremacy into a literal, futile ascent. | terra: Pharaoh asks Haman for a lofty structure so he may reach the routes, staging political greatness as an attempted ascent.

luna: The section contrasts true divine height with a ruler’s claim; this neighbor completes Pharaoh’s tower order by showing its failure and his delusion about Moses’ God. | terra: The requested routes lead toward the heavens so Pharaoh can look at Moses' God, but his scheme only bars him from the way; literal ascent exposes spiritual lowness.

luna: The section opposes the low worldly life to the lasting Hereafter; this verse calls the worldly life a temporary enjoyment and the Hereafter the enduring home. | terra: Worldly life is a temporary enjoyment, while the hereafter is دَارُ ٱلْقَرَارِ, the lasting home.
terra: Those disputing God's signs harbor only كِبْرٌۭ مَّا هُم بِبَٰلِغِيهِ, a greatness they will never attain; the ayah states the failure inside their upward claim.
terra: Entering Hell's gates is again called the dwelling of the arrogant, a repeated Quranic judgment on creaturely greatness.

luna: The section’s d-n-w gloss includes the nearer thing and its ʿ-l-w axis the highest; this verse names the nearest heaven and describes its adornment, making the same vertical scale cosmic. | terra: وَزَيَّنَّا ٱلسَّمَآءَ ٱلدُّنْيَا again uses الدنيا for the nearest heaven, separating the root's spatial nearness from its moral valuation of life.

luna: The section’s axis assigns true height to God; this verse calls Him “العلي العظيم,” a direct divine height-and-greatness formula. | terra: Ownership of heaven and earth belongs to God, وَهُوَ ٱلْعَلِىُّ ٱلْعَظِيمُ; the title rests on possession rather than assertion.
terra: The heavens nearly rupture from above while angels glorify their Lord, turning the divine height of 42:4 into cosmic tasbih.
terra: Whoever seeks the harvest of the hereafter receives increase, while the seeker of worldly harvest receives only some of it and no final share.

luna: The section says the low, near worldly life is outweighed by the better and more enduring Hereafter; this verse uses that same comparison and specifies that what is with God is better and more lasting. | terra: What people receive is only enjoyment of worldly life, while what is with God is خَيْرٌۭ وَأَبْقَىٰ for believers.
terra: The account of how God speaks to humans ends by naming Him High and Wise, grounding descending revelation in the exaltation of its speaker.
terra: The Quran is in the Mother of the Book with God, exalted and wise; revealed remembrance itself receives a true high station.
terra: God apportions worldly livelihood and raises some above others in degrees for mutual service, yet His mercy is better than what they accumulate; worldly rank is relativized within the ayah.
terra: Gold and worldly luxury are reduced to mere enjoyment, while the hereafter with the Lord belongs to the God-fearing.
terra: وَإِنَّهُۥ لَذِكْرٌۭ لَّكَ وَلِقَوْمِكَ explicitly makes revelation a remembrance or honor for the Prophet and his people, matching dhikr's elevated secondary sense.

luna: The section’s image opposes true highness to a ruler’s self-claimed supremacy; Pharaoh boasts of his kingdom and the rivers beneath him, grounding his status claim in worldly dominion. | terra: Pharaoh proclaims his Egyptian dominion and visible rivers, using assembled worldly spectacle to support the superiority claimed in 79:24.

luna: The section presents Pharaoh as claiming the highest place; this neighbor completes his boast by belittling Moses as insignificant and barely able to make himself clear. | terra: Pharaoh calls Moses مَهِينٌ and scarcely articulate, pushing his rival downward in the same speech by which he elevates himself.
terra: Pharaoh makes his people light or foolish and they obey him; the social mechanism of his claimed superiority is the lowering of those beneath him.
terra: The Lord of heavens, earth, and Throne is glorified above what they describe, joining cosmic height to transcendence from false speech.
terra: Pharaoh is called عَالِيًۭا مِّنَ ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ as Israel is delivered from his humiliating punishment, joining height-claim to excess.
terra: People made God's signs an object of ridicule and were deceived by worldly life; the low horizon becomes the agent of their false estimate.

luna: The section contrasts God’s true greatness with human self-magnification; this verse says greatness in the heavens and earth belongs to God, placing the grandeur claimed by rulers under divine ownership. | terra: وَلَهُ ٱلْكِبْرِيَآءُ فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ assigns الكبرياء throughout creation to God, setting the rightful possession of greatness against human pretension.
terra: People exhaust their good things in worldly life and act arrogantly on earth; humiliating punishment joins the low-life choice to counterfeit elevation.
terra: وَأَنتُمُ ٱلْأَعْلَوْنَ وَٱللَّهُ مَعَكُمْ grounds the believers' upper hand in God's presence, not self-magnification.
terra: Worldly life is play and diversion, whereas faith and reverence receive their reward; present possession is denied the power to measure true rank.
terra: Glorification with the Lord's praise is commanded before sunrise and sunset, joining the speaker stance to the horizon imagery developed in the section.
terra: The oath by ٱلسَّقْفِ ٱلْمَرْفُوعِ presents heaven as a raised roof, a creaturely height that points beyond itself.
terra: The question whether they possess a god other than God ends by glorifying Him above their partners, reserving lordship and height for Him.
terra: While standing under the Lord's watch, the Prophet is commanded to glorify Him with praise; worship, stance, and divine oversight meet.
terra: Night glorification and the retreat of the stars extend the command of 52:48 into the celestial scene.
terra: The revelation is taught by one mighty in power, identifying the agent whose strength, stance, and appearance at the high horizon are described in 53:6-7.

luna: The section evokes a shape rising into view; this preceding verse describes the figure as mighty and upright, while 53:7 supplies the highest horizon that completes the silhouette scene. | terra: The revelation-bearer is described as ذُو مِرَّةٍۢ and standing poised; this gives the figure whose appearance on the high horizon follows in 53:7.

luna: The section’s s-m-w dictionary branch describes a figure rising above the horizon until it can be made out; this verse places the figure at “الأفق الأعلى,” giving that horizon-and-height image a Quranic scene. | terra: وَهُوَ بِٱلْأُفُقِ ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ realizes the dictionary image of a figure becoming distinct at the high horizon.

luna: The section’s horizon image can be read as a figure seen at a distance; after 53:7 places him at the highest horizon, this verse says he drew near and descended, changing distance within the same scene. | terra: ثُمَّ دَنَا فَتَدَلَّىٰ follows the figure at the highest horizon with drawing near and descending; height and nearness become movements in one vision.

luna: The section’s s-m-w branch is about a rising figure made visible; this neighbor measures the approach described in 53:8 as two bow-lengths or nearer, adding scale to the horizon scene. | terra: أَوْ أَدْنَىٰ measures an even nearer distance, completing the motion from the high horizon rather than treating “near” as low in worth.
luna: The section connects the horizon figure with revelation; this neighbor completes the approach of 53:8–9 by saying revelation came to His servant.
terra: The idols are only names coined by people and their fathers without authority, another boundary between a raised sound and a real divine referent.

luna: The section connects remembrance of the Lord’s name to choosing the low worldly life; this verse sets turning away from remembrance beside desiring only the life of this world, making the choice a rejection of remembrance. | terra: The Prophet must turn from one who turns from God's reminder and desires only worldly life; dhikr and low-life preference are direct alternatives.
terra: That worldly horizon is called the limit of their knowledge, while the Lord knows who strays and who is guided; nearness confines understanding as well as desire.
terra: وَٱلسَّمَآءَ رَفَعَهَا and the setting of the balance make height a created order rather than a boast.

luna: The section joins the Lord’s name to exaltation and honor; this verse blesses the name of the Lord who possesses majesty and honor, making the name itself the site of that reverence. | terra: تَبَٰرَكَ ٱسْمُ رَبِّكَ ذِى ٱلْجَلَٰلِ وَٱلْإِكْرَامِ makes the Lord's name itself the locus of blessing, majesty, and honor.
terra: The coming event is خَافِضَةٌۭ رَّافِعَةٌۭ, lowering and raising; it turns the section's lexical axis into an eschatological reversal of rank.

luna: The section’s tasbīḥ gloss supplies the act and its k-b-r gloss the divine magnification; this same command to glorify the great Lord names both, though it does not add the word “name” found in 87:1. | terra: فَسَبِّحْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلْعَظِيمِ repeats the section's command, Lord, name, and glorification while replacing “Most High” with “Magnificent.”

luna: The section says tasbīḥ is declaring God free of every evil and links the great-fire word’s k-b-r family to magnifying God; this command joins glorification to the Lord’s name and greatness in one phrase. | terra: The surah closes by repeating فَسَبِّحْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلْعَظِيمِ, making glorification through the Lord's name the response to its final certainties.

luna: The section makes tasbīḥ the act of declaring God free of every evil; this verse opens with everything in the heavens and earth glorifying Him, extending the named act to the whole created scene.
terra: Worldly life is play, adornment, boasting, and rivalry in increase, then vegetation that dries and becomes debris; apparent greatness ends in disappearance.
terra: After worldly growth and debris in 57:20, believers are told to race toward forgiveness and a garden as wide as heaven and earth, supplying the enduring destination beyond the fading scene.

luna: The section’s al-ʿulūw image treats highness as a bestowed rank; this verse says God raises those who believe and those given knowledge by degrees, clarifying that genuine rank is granted, not seized. | terra: God يَرْفَعِ believers and people of knowledge دَرَجَٰتٍۢ, showing elevation as a divine award joined to faith and understanding.

luna: The section’s k-b-r dictionary gloss gives greatness and also permits self-inflated grandeur; this verse names God “المتكبر” and immediately glorifies Him above partners, separating divine majesty from a creature’s claim. | terra: God alone is ٱلْمُتَكَبِّرُ and سُبْحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ clears Him of partners; the ayah distinguishes divine greatness from the blameworthy greatness creatures assume.

luna: The section joins the Lord’s name to glorification; this verse says the beautiful names belong to God and that all in the heavens and earth glorify Him, joining the two acts named in 87:1 and 87:15. | terra: The Creator has ٱلْأَسْمَآءُ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ and everything glorifies Him, directly bringing creation, names, and tasbih together.
terra: The call to prayer requires hastening to ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ and leaving trade, staging remembered worship against immediate worldly gain.
terra: People leave the Messenger standing for trade or amusement, but مَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ خَيْرٌۭ; the scene exposes the low-life preference that 62:9 had interrupted.
terra: When told تَعَالَوْا۟ يَسْتَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ, hypocrites turn their heads in pride; they refuse an upward-form call because of self-elevation.
terra: Wealth and children must not distract believers from God's remembrance; immediate attachments and dhikr are presented as competing orientations.
terra: Wealth and children are only a trial, while a great reward is with God; possessed greatness is subordinated to bestowed greatness.

luna: The section contrasts the high with the low or near; this verse calls the nearest heaven “السماء الدنيا,” giving that low/near pole a literal place in the sky and contrasting it with the section’s highest heavens. | terra: ٱلسَّمَآءَ ٱلدُّنْيَا is adorned with lamps, placing the “nearest” term in a luminous heaven and exposing the root sense beneath worldly usage.
terra: The recipient of the right-hand record enters a high garden, making eschatological height the outcome of accepted life rather than claimed status.
terra: The high garden's fruit clusters are near, joining height and nearness as harmonized gifts and contrasting this nearness with the morally low worldly life.

luna: The section links “سَبِّح” to declaring God above every evil and identifies k-b-r with magnifying Him; this verse explicitly commands glorification by the name of the Great Lord, matching 87:1’s name-and-praise. | terra: فَسَبِّحْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلْعَظِيمِ is the same command-frame as 87:1 and again makes the named Lord, rather than a creature, the bearer of greatness.

luna: The section joins the Lord’s name with remembrance and prayer; this command to remember the Lord’s name and devote oneself to Him gives that pairing a night-worship setting. | terra: وَٱذْكُرِ ٱسْمَ رَبِّكَ is the direct counterpart of remembering the Lord's name in 87:15 and makes that remembrance an undivided turning to Him.
terra: وَرَبَّكَ فَكَبِّرْ is the Quranic act named by the section's dictionary note on takbir: ascribe greatness to the Lord.

luna: The section’s k-b-r gloss distinguishes true greatness from self-claimed grandeur; this verse depicts a person turning away and “استكبر,” a concrete form of false elevation before he rejects the reminder.
terra: The warned fire is called إِحْدَى ٱلْكُبَرِ, one of the greatest things, giving the fire's greatness root an explicitly eschatological referent.

luna: The section’s d-n-w gloss includes what is nearest; this verse names the immediate life (“العاجلة”) as what people love, sharpening the temporal-nearness side of its low-life image. | terra: بَلْ تُحِبُّونَ ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ restates preference for the nearer life without using دنيا: they love what comes immediately.

luna: The section opposes the near life to the better, lasting Hereafter; this neighbor completes 75:20 by saying they leave the Hereafter, making the preference explicit. | terra: وَتَذَرُونَ ٱلْءَاخِرَةَ names what is abandoned when the immediate is loved in 75:20.
terra: Garden shade draws near and its fruit clusters are lowered within reach; true nearness is received through a merciful lowering in the final abode.

luna: The section’s name-and-remembrance pairing is repeated here as a command to remember the Lord’s name morning and evening, extending the act across the day. | terra: وَٱذْكُرِ ٱسْمَ رَبِّكَ commands remembrance of the Lord's name, matching the wording and stance of 87:15.
terra: Prostration and long glorification at night enact the worship commanded in 76:25, joining remembrance of the name to bodily lowering before the exalted Lord.
terra: They love ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ and leave a weighty day behind them, another nonlexical formulation of choosing nearness over the final horizon.

luna: The section contrasts the Lord’s true highness with a creature’s claim to be highest; Pharaoh’s “الأعلى” is precisely that usurped title, so the scene makes false elevation answerable to the One glorified in 87:1. | terra: Pharaoh says أَنَا۠ رَبُّكُمُ ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ; a creature seizes both “Lord” and “Most High,” staging the section's corrupted elevation.
terra: God seizes Pharaoh with punishment of the later and the former; the consequence immediately overturns his claim to be the highest lord and restores the two-life scale.
terra: Pharaoh's reversal is made an admonitory sign for whoever fears, linking the cited scene to the fear that receives reminder in Surah 87.
terra: The question whether humans are harder to create than the heaven God built redirects attention from Pharaoh's assumed height to the Creator of actual height.
terra: رَفَعَ سَمْكَهَا فَسَوَّىٰهَا describes God raising and proportioning heaven shortly after Pharaoh's false “Most High” claim in the same surah.
terra: The coming overwhelming event is called the greatest catastrophe, placing the greatness root immediately before remembrance, exposed Hell, and the low-life choice.
terra: On that day the human being remembers what he strove for; remembrance now discloses the life-choice whose judgment follows.
terra: Hell is made plainly visible to every observer just before the one who transgressed and preferred worldly life is identified.

luna: The section’s ʿ-l-w dictionary gloss says that rising in the land can mean transgressing and magnifying oneself; this is the verdict on the one who “طغى,” the corrupt earthly height that the divine name displaces. | terra: The judgment begins with مَن طَغَىٰ, naming the transgression embodied by Pharaoh's claim in 79:24 and preparing the low-life choice in the next ayah.

luna: The section’s d-n-w gloss makes “الدنيا” the low, lesser, or nearer thing; this verse repeats the precise choice in 87:16, “آثر الحياة الدنيا,” inside the same judgment scene as Pharaoh’s transgression. | terra: وَءَاثَرَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا exactly joins preference to the low/near life, as in 87:16, and identifies the choice beneath counterfeit height.

luna: The section sets choosing the low worldly life against the Hereafter; this neighbor completes 79:38 by making the Fire the transgressor’s refuge, matching 87:12’s great Fire as the consequence of that choice. | terra: Hell becomes the refuge of the one who transgressed and preferred the low life in 79:37-38, supplying the consequence corresponding to 87:12.

luna: The section’s opposite poles are the low worldly preference and the Lord’s highness; this neighbor turns to the one who fears standing before his Lord and restrains desire, completing the reversal begun at 79:37–39 and echoing 87:10. | terra: Fearing the station before the Lord and restraining desire reverses 79:37-38: true regard for the Lord checks the self that chooses the nearer life.

luna: The section says the Hereafter is better and more enduring than the low, near life; this neighbor completes 79:40’s restraint with the Garden as refuge, the enduring alternative to 79:39’s Fire. | terra: The Garden is the refuge of the one described in 79:40, completing the opposite outcome to Hell in 79:39.

luna: The section’s dh-k-r dictionary gloss includes honor and high mention, while the surah also centers reminder; this verse calls the message a reminder, showing the related but distinct admonitory sense.
luna: The section links remembrance to honor; this neighbor specifies that whoever wills may remember the reminder introduced in 80:11, rather than treating the word as only public renown.
luna: The section’s remembrance-and-elevation image has a textual counterpart in this continuation: the reminder is in honored pages, giving the act of remembering a dignified setting.
luna: The section’s s-m-w imagery is elevation and its dh-k-r gloss is honor; this neighbor calls those pages “مرفوعة مطهرة,” joining elevation to purity.

luna: The section’s elevation and honor image continues here: 80:15 places the pages in the hands of scribes, and this verse calls their bearers noble and dutiful, specifying the honored setting introduced in 80:13.
terra: The discourse is the word conveyed by a noble messenger, identifying the same revelation-bearer whose horizon appearance is stated in 81:23.
terra: The messenger has power and an established station with the Lord of the Throne, giving rightful rank and strength to the figure seen on the horizon.

luna: The section’s s-m-w branch evokes a shape emerging at the horizon and becoming visible; here the seen figure is “بالأفق المبين,” a direct horizon scene that clarifies the branch’s visual sense. | terra: The Prophet saw the messenger on the clear horizon, a direct parallel to the high-horizon figure in 53:7 and to the dictionary's emerging silhouette.
terra: The record of the righteous is in عِلِّيِّينَ, an explicitly high register contrasted with the wicked record in Sijjin.
terra: The question وَمَآ أَدْرَىٰكَ مَا عِلِّيُّونَ marks the high register as a reality needing disclosure, not a self-claimed rank.
terra: A written register defines what Illiyyun contains, giving content to the high designation introduced in 83:18.
terra: Those brought near witness the high register, joining true nearness to the righteous height of 83:18.

luna: The section’s s-m-w branch names the crescent rising above the horizon; this verse swears by the moon when full, a later visible phase that completes the crescent’s growth rather than repeating the crescent itself.
terra: Faces are humbled on the coming day, an eschatological lowering that strips away assumed worldly elevation.
terra: Those humbled faces enter a scorching fire, supplying the fire-side of the passage's later contrast with a high garden.
terra: Other faces are in a high garden, giving true height as an awarded final dwelling opposite the humbled faces and fire.
terra: Raised couches furnish the high garden, making its elevation a concrete created gift rather than a human claim.
terra: The hearer is asked to look at the sky كَيْفَ رُفِعَتْ, directing attention from visible height to the act of its raising.

luna: The section’s s-m-w branch evokes the crescent becoming visible as it rises above the horizon; this verse stages the moon following the sun, a specific paired movement across the sky that frames that rising image.

luna: The section’s 87:11–15 sequence sets the one who avoids reminder and burns in the great Fire against the one who purifies and remembers; this verse opens a parallel warning with the blazing Fire. | terra: A blazing fire is announced just before the purified giver is kept from it and seeks the face of his Most High Lord in 92:17-20.
luna: The section names the “أشقى” who burns in 87:12; this neighbor specifies that none but the most wretched will burn in the Fire introduced at 92:14.

luna: The section contrasts the person who fears and remembers with one who avoids the reminder; this neighbor identifies the one who denies and turns away as the one who burns in the paired scene of 92:14–15.

luna: The section contrasts those who turn from reminder and face the great Fire with the one who purifies and remembers; this verse says the most God-fearing will be kept from that Fire, the reverse fate in the same moral image. | terra: The most God-fearing is kept away from the blazing fire of 92:14, preparing the purification and Most High Lord of the following ayat.

luna: The section pairs purification with remembrance and prayer; this neighbor identifies the person who gives his wealth in order to purify himself, the concrete act behind the aim at 92:20 and 87:14. | terra: The giver spends wealth يَتَزَكَّىٰ, joining purification to the movement toward the Most High Lord named in 92:20.

luna: The section opposes the low, near worldly preference to devotion to the highest Lord; this neighbor says the giver seeks no repayment for a favor, clarifying that the giving at 92:18 is not a worldly exchange. | terra: No person's favor is being repaid by the giver; this excludes a lower reciprocal motive before 92:20 names the Most High Lord as his sole aim.

luna: The section explicitly cites this aim: seeking the face of the “الأعلى” Lord. Its ʿ-l-w axis therefore distinguishes the giver’s devotion to God from a worldly claim to be highest. | terra: The purified giver seeks only وَجْهِ رَبِّهِ ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ; “Most High” names the Lord as the enduring object chosen over recompense or possession.

luna: The section says the Hereafter is better and more enduring; this neighbor completes the giving and God-directed aim of 92:18–20 with the promised satisfaction. | terra: The giver who seeks the face of his Most High Lord will be satisfied, completing the movement beyond wealth and human recompense.
terra: وَلَلْءَاخِرَةُ خَيْرٌۭ لَّكَ مِنَ ٱلْأُولَىٰ states the same better-later valuation without using دنيا, sharpening the temporal dimension of low/near.

luna: The section’s dh-k-r dictionary gloss calls remembrance “highness and honor”; 94:4 says God raised the Prophet’s remembrance, making the section’s elevation audible as honor rather than physical height. | terra: وَرَفَعْنَا لَكَ ذِكْرَكَ states the section's dictionary relation literally: remembrance or renown is raised.
terra: Humanity is returned أَسْفَلَ سَٰفِلِينَ after creation in the best form, a stark downward reversal that makes moral height contingent.

luna: The section treats the Lord’s “name” as a bearer of elevated mention; this command to read by the name of the Lord who created connects that name to the Creator praised at the opening of 87. | terra: ٱقْرَأْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ joins the Lord's name to the command and to creation, as 87:1-2 joins glorifying the name to the Creator.

luna: The section says ʿ-l-w can mean transgressing and magnifying oneself; this verse says the human being transgresses when he sees himself self-sufficient, locating false height in imagined independence. | terra: The human being transgresses, introducing the counterfeit upward motion inside the surah that began by naming the creating Lord.

luna: The section exposes self-exalting height as corrupt; this neighbor completes 96:6 by stating the trigger for that transgression, the person’s sense that he has no need. | terra: Seeing himself self-sufficient explains the transgression in 96:6; imagined independence is the inward form of claiming height for oneself.
terra: The return is to your Lord, setting the final horizon above the self-sufficiency that produced transgression in 96:6-7.
terra: وَٱسْجُدْ وَٱقْتَرِب joins bodily lowering in prostration to true nearness, a concrete reversal of seeking elevation for oneself.
terra: At the moment of victory the Prophet must glorify his Lord with praise and seek forgiveness, preventing success from becoming self-elevation.
